title: [Feature/Graphics]: Software 2D BSP Tree Doom-Style Sector Portal Renderer with Textured Floors
body:
## Problem
Classic 1993 FPS engines achieved non-orthogonal rooms, varying ceiling heights, and fast overdraw occlusion on CPUs using Binary Space Partitioning (BSP) trees and column/span clipping—an extraordinary graphics engineering challenge absent from ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 380+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/bsp-sector-renderer.js`:
     - Implement static 2D BSP tree builder splitting arbitrary non-orthogonal line segments (`linedefs`) into convex sub-sectors along partition planes.
     - Implement front-to-back BSP traversal relative to camera `(x, y, yaw)` with solid horizontal 1D occlusion buffer (`screenCovered[x]`) + upper/lower portal height clipping (`topY[x]`, `bottomY[x]`).
     - Render procedural pixel-buffer textured walls, distance fog attenuation, and basic floor/ceiling color spans into a 2D Canvas `ImageData` buffer at smooth interactive framerates alongside a synchronized top-down 2D BSP split-plane minimap and WASD/Arrow movement!
   - Create `assets/css/bsp-sector-renderer.css`:
     - Split viewport (320x200 upscaled crisp 2.5D Canvas + 2D BSP partition tree minimap), map preset selector (`Hub Arena`, `Spiral Hall`, `Multi-Elevation Courtyard`), and live FPS / rendered sub-sector stats.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas `ImageData` (**NO WebGL/Three.js**), zero external libraries, zero emojis.
3. Add automated unit test `scripts/test-bsp-sector-renderer.js` verifying point-vs-line side classification (`cross2D`), BSP segment splitting math without degenerate zero-length fragments, and front-to-back traversal ordering invariants.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] BSP traversal renders non-orthogonal angled rooms and varying ceiling elevations cleanly with zero overdraw flicker.
- [ ] Top-down minimap highlights visible BSP sub-sectors live as the camera moves and rotates.
- [ ] Runs smoothly via pure software pixel writes (`ImageData`) with zero WebGL dependencies.
- [ ] Total new code exceeds 380 meaningful lines across isolated files without modifying protected files.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-bsp-sector-renderer.js` passes under `node`.

title: [Feature/Physics]: 2D Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics Liquid Fluid and Dam-Break Solver
body:
## Problem
Grid-based smoke solvers look airy, whereas Lagrangian particle fluid simulation (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics — SPH) models realistic incompressible liquid splashing, surface tension, and dam-break waves interacting with rigid walls.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 320+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/sph-fluid-solver.js`:
     - Implement 2D SPH fluid physics across `300`–`800` liquid particles using an O(N) uniform spatial-hash neighbor grid (never slow O(N^2) brute force!).
     - Implement Poly6 density kernel, Spiky pressure gradient force (`F_pressure`), and viscosity Laplacian force (`F_viscosity`) with Leapfrog/Symplectic Euler integration and wall boundary clamping.
     - Include interactive Dam-Break gate release button, interactive pointer push/scoop vortex tool, Gravity tilt angle control, and smooth velocity-colored liquid rendering.
   - Create `assets/css/sph-fluid-solver.css`:
     - Tank canvas container with controls for Target Rest Density, Gas Stiffness, Viscosity, Gravity Tilt, Dam Reset, and live neighbor-lookup performance telemetry.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas, zero external physics engines, zero emojis.
3. Add comprehensive test suite `scripts/test-sph-fluid-solver.js` validating Poly6 & Spiky kernel boundary behavior (`W(r >= h) === 0`), spatial hash cell neighbor completeness vs brute-force equivalence, and finite non-NaN velocity bounds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Spatial-hash neighbor grid enables hundreds of liquid particles to splash and settle smoothly at interactive framerates.
- [ ] Dam-break gate release creates realistic surging liquid waves and hydrostatic pressure equilibrium.
- [ ] Spatial hash neighbor lookup test proves 100% parity with exact brute-force within radius `h`.
- [ ] Implementation exceeds 320 meaningful lines across isolated files without touching protected core files.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-sph-fluid-solver.js` passes under `node`.

title: [Feature/Physics]: 2D Bridge Truss Tension Stress Heatmap and Vehicle Load Physics Simulator
body:
## Problem
Engineering bridge-builder sandboxes let players construct triangular trusses, inspect real-time tension vs compression stress color maps, and drive physics vehicles across spans to test structural integrity—an engaging physics sandbox absent from ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 360+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/bridge-truss-sim.js`:
     - Build interactive node-and-beam construction grid over a canyon chasm (Fixed Anchor Joints, Free Joints, Road Deck Beams, Steel Support Struts, Tension Cables) with cost budget tracking and 2 pre-built sample bridges (Arch Truss & Warren Truss).
     - Implement constraint-relaxation / spring-damper truss physics solver tracking exact axial stretch/compression ratio per beam: coloring beams smoothly from Cool Blue (compression) -> Neutral Grey -> Bright Crimson (near snapping threshold!) and snapping overloaded links cleanly.
     - Simulate a 2-wheel spring-suspension test buggy that drives across road deck beams applying dynamic rolling downward weight!
   - Create `assets/css/bridge-truss-sim.css`:
     - Build/Test mode switch, material palette, Budget meter, `"Drive Test Vehicle"` button, and stress legend.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas, zero external physics libraries, zero emojis.
3. Add automated unit test `scripts/test-bridge-truss-sim.js` verifying beam stress ratio sign (`tension > 0`, `compression < 0`), snap fracture removal above breaking strain, anchor pinning invariance, and budget calculation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Players can build, erase, and test custom truss bridges with live tension/compression stress heatmaps.
- [ ] Driving the physics vehicle visibly flexes road beams and snaps overloaded struts realistically.
- [ ] Sample pre-built Warren Truss supports the vehicle cleanly across the canyon gap.
- [ ] Total new code exceeds 360 meaningful lines across isolated files with zero protected file changes.

title: [Feature/Graphics]: Software 3D Textured Scanline Triangle Rasterizer with Perspective Texture Mapping
body:
## Problem
Building a pure CPU software 3D triangle rasterizer from scratch—handling homogeneous clipping, edge-equation/scanline interpolation, per-pixel Z-buffering, and `1/z` perspective-correct UV texture mapping—is a landmark graphics engineering challenge missing from ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 360+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/software-rasterizer-3d.js`:
     - Implement 4x4 perspective projection & model-view matrix pipeline (`perspective`, `lookAt`, `rotateXYZ`), backface culling, and screen-space bounding/scanline triangle rasterizer writing directly into `ImageData` + `Float32Array` Z-buffer.
     - Support 3 selectable shading modes highlighting historical rendering quirks: `Affine UV` (classic PS1 texture warping!), `Perspective-Correct (u/z, v/z, 1/z)` crisp mapping, and `Gouraud Vertex Lit`, using procedural checkerboard/brick/circuit textures generated in memory.
     - Include selectable 3D meshes (`Textured Cube`, `Octahedron`, `Subdivided Sphere`, `Torus`) with pointer orbit rotation and wireframe overlay toggle.
   - Create `assets/css/software-rasterizer-3d.css`:
     - Crisp rasterizer Canvas viewport (`320x240` or `400x300` upscaled), shading mode radio pills, Z-buffer visualization toggle, and triangle/pixel throughput stats.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas `ImageData` (**strictly NO WebGL/Three.js**), zero external packages, zero emojis.
3. Add comprehensive test suite `scripts/test-software-rasterizer-3d.js` verifying 4x4 matrix multiplication identity/inverses, barycentric weight sum `== 1.0`, Z-buffer closer-pixel overwrite rule, and backface winding sign checks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Perspective-correct UV mapping renders distortion-free textured 3D meshes, visibly contrasting against Affine PS1 warping mode.
- [ ] Per-pixel Z-buffer accurately resolves intersecting meshes without sorting glitches.
- [ ] Optional Z-buffer depth map view renders clean grayscale depth gradients.
- [ ] Total implementation exceeds 360 meaningful lines without modifying protected core files.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-software-rasterizer-3d.js` passes under `node`.

title: [Feature/Algorithms]: Exact Cover Dancing Links DLX Toroidal Matrix Solver Visualizer
body:
## Problem
Donald Knuth's Algorithm X using Dancing Links (DLX) solves NP-complete exact cover puzzles (Sudoku, N-Queens, Pentomino Tiling) exponentially faster than naive backtracking through O(1) doubly-linked circular node cover/uncover operations—yet few developers ever get to see the toroidal matrix dance live.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 300+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/dancing-links-dlx.js`:
     - Implement genuine circular doubly-linked toroidal matrix (`DLXNode` with `L, R, U, D, C` column headers + MRV `S` minimum-remaining-values heuristic) and reversible `cover(col)` / `uncover(col)` operations.
     - Implement exact-cover encoders for BOTH **Classic 9x9 Sudoku** (324 constraint columns!) AND **N-Queens (`N=4..8`)** / **Custom Binary Matrix**.
     - Emit step-by-step solver trace events (`choose_col`, `try_row`, `backtrack`, `solution_found`) animating cell fills, backtracking erasures, and matrix cover/uncover stats in real-time!
   - Create `assets/css/dancing-links-dlx.css`:
     - Split view displaying interactive Sudoku/N-Queens board (editable presets + custom entry), step-by-step animation speed slider, and live DLX recursion depth / node unlink-relink counters.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/CSS3, zero external solver packages, zero emojis.
3. Add unit test `scripts/test-dancing-links-dlx.js` verifying reversible `cover`/`uncover` pointer invariants, exact cover solution correctness on tricky 9x9 Sudokus (`17-clue` / hard presets), and exact solution count for 4-Queens (`2`) and 8-Queens (`92`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Authentic circular doubly-linked DLX matrix solves hard 9x9 Sudokus and enumerates exact N-Queens solution counts (`N=8 -> 92`).
- [ ] Visual stepper animates column selection, tentative placements, and instant backtracking cleanly.
- [ ] Cover/uncover pointer restoration leaves zero corrupted links after full search completion.
- [ ] Codebase exceeds 300 meaningful lines across isolated files without editing protected core files.
- [ ] Unit test `scripts/test-dancing-links-dlx.js` passes under `node`.

title: [Feature/Graphics]: Procedural 2D Differential Line Growth and Organic Coral Folding Engine
body:
## Problem
Biological morphogenesis patterns like brain coral, lichen ruffles, and leaf margins form via differential line growth: a closed elastic curve whose segments subdivide whenever edge length exceeds a threshold while nearby non-adjacent nodes repel each other.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 250+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/differential-growth.js`:
     - Implement closed/open node-chain data structure with spring attraction to immediate neighbors, inverse-square spatial-hash repulsion from nearby nodes within radius `R`, and dynamic midpoint node splitting (`edgeLen > maxEdgeLen`) capped safely (`maxNodes = 2500`).
     - Support multiple seed shapes (`Circle Ring`, `Star Polygon`, `Multiple Merging Rings`) plus interactive cursor `"Food/Nutrient"` growth modulation (nodes grow faster where painted!) and smooth Catmull-Rom / quadratic midpoint curve rendering.
   - Create `assets/css/differential-growth.css`:
     - Studio viewport with sliders for Repulsion Radius, Spring Tension, Split Threshold, Color Gradient (`Coral Reef`, `Bioluminescent`, `Ink Contour`), Play/Pause, and `"Export SVG"` download button.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas/SVG, zero external packages, zero emojis.
3. Add automated test `scripts/test-differential-growth.js` verifying spatial-hash collision avoidance, midpoint insertion preserving closed ring topology, max-node memory safety cap enforcement, and valid closed SVG `<path>` serialization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Spatial hashing keeps 1,500+ folding coral nodes animating smoothly without quadratic lag.
- [ ] Edges subdivide smoothly without self-intersecting tangles under default presets.
- [ ] Max-node cap and SVG export work reliably across desktop and mobile.
- [ ] Total new code exceeds 250 lines across isolated files without modifying protected files.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-differential-growth.js` passes under `node`.

title: [Feature/Physics]: Interactive 2D Lattice-Boltzmann D2Q9 Wind Tunnel Airfoil Vorticity Lab
body:
## Problem
Lattice-Boltzmann Methods (LBM D2Q9) simulate real compressible/low-Mach wind tunnel aerodynamics—producing textbook Karman vortex streets behind cylinders and airfoils—using local lattice streaming and BGK collision without global Poisson pressure solves.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 300+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/lbm-wind-tunnel.js`:
     - Implement standard D2Q9 Lattice-Boltzmann solver across a 2D grid (`e_0..e_8` discrete lattice velocities in `Float32Array`), performing BGK equilibrium collision (`tau` viscosity relaxation), streaming step, bounce-back solid barrier boundary conditions, and Zou-He left-wall wind inflow velocity!
     - Render real-time Curl/Vorticity (`dv/dx - du/dy` blue-black-red diverging colormap) OR Wind Speed / Tracer streamlines into Canvas `ImageData`.
     - Provide preset obstacles (`Cylinder`, `NACA Airfoil`, `Flat Plate`) PLUS interactive mouse brush letting users draw/erase custom wind tunnel barriers live while watching Karman vortex shedding form!
   - Create `assets/css/lbm-wind-tunnel.css`:
     - Wind tunnel viewport with Wind Speed (`u0`), Viscosity (`omega`), Visualization Mode (`Vorticity Curl` vs `Velocity Speed`), Brush Tool, and stability clamp monitor.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/Canvas `ImageData`, zero external CFD/WebGL packages, zero emojis.
3. Add unit test `scripts/test-lbm-wind-tunnel.js` validating D2Q9 equilibrium weight normalization (`sum(w_i) === 1.0`), local mass conservation (`sum(f_i)` unchanged by BGK collision), and exact velocity reversal on bounce-back solid barriers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] D2Q9 wind tunnel produces clear Karman vortex streets behind cylinders and tilted airfoils at interactive framerates.
- [ ] Drawing or erasing solid barriers updates bounce-back flow wakes instantaneously.
- [ ] Equilibrium mass conservation and bounce-back unit tests pass with machine precision.
- [ ] Codebase exceeds 300 meaningful lines across isolated files without editing protected core files.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-lbm-wind-tunnel.js` passes under `node`.

title: [Feature/Algorithms]: Interactive Force-Directed Graph Layout with Kruskal MST and Max-Flow Stepper
body:
## Problem
Understanding weighted graph algorithms like Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree (using Disjoint-Set Union-Find) and Edmonds-Karp Maximum Flow (augmenting paths + residual graphs) is vastly easier when combined with an interactive draggable force-directed graph editor.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 280+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/graph-algo-workbench.js`:
     - Implement interactive graph editor supporting node add/drag/delete, weighted directed/undirected edge creation, random planar-ish graph generator, and Fruchterman-Reingold spring-electric force-directed auto-layout!
     - Implement step-by-step animated algorithms:
       - **Kruskal's MST** with explicit Disjoint-Set (`UnionFind` with path compression & union by rank) highlighting accepted vs cycle-rejected edges.
       - **Edmonds-Karp Max-Flow** highlighting live augmenting BFS path, bottleneck capacity, and `flow / capacity` labels per edge!
   - Create `assets/css/graph-algo-workbench.css`:
     - Canvas graph editor with mode tools (`Move`, `Add Node`, `Add Edge`, `Set Source/Sink`), algorithm selector, Step/Run controls, and total MST weight / Max Flow readout.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas/CSS3, zero external graph libraries (no D3/Cytoscape), zero emojis.
3. Add automated test `scripts/test-graph-algo-workbench.js` validating `UnionFind` cycle detection, Kruskal MST exact minimum total weight on canonical test graphs, and Edmonds-Karp Max-Flow Min-Cut parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Force-directed layout settles tangled graphs smoothly while allowing live node dragging.
- [ ] Stepper visibly animates Kruskal Union-Find decisions and Edmonds-Karp residual flow updates.
- [ ] Both algorithms produce mathematically exact totals verified by unit tests.
- [ ] Total new code exceeds 280 lines across isolated files without touching protected files.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-graph-algo-workbench.js` passes under `node`.

title: [Feature/Graphics]: Software 2D Raytraced Reflective Mirror and Snells Law Prism Dispersion Sandbox
body:
## Problem
Real-time 2D geometric optics—tracing rays through angled mirrors, dielectric glass blocks, circular lenses, and refractive prisms that split white light into rainbow spectra via wavelength-dependent Snell's Law dispersion—creates a captivating physics & graphics sandbox missing from ArcadeVerse.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 280+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/optics-prism-sandbox.js`:
     - Implement exact analytical ray-segment and ray-circle intersection solver supporting iterative reflection/refraction ray tree expansion (depth cap `<= 8` bounces) using Snell's Law `n1*sin(theta1) = n2*sin(theta2)`, Fresnel reflectance splitting, and Total Internal Reflection (TIR)!
     - Implement multi-wavelength Cauchy chromatic dispersion (`7` spectral bands Red -> Violet with slightly shifting refractive indices `n(lambda)`) so white laser beams fan into vibrant rainbow spectra exiting triangular glass prisms!
     - Allow dragging/rotating Mirrors, Triangular Prisms, Biconvex Lenses, and Laser Emitters directly on Canvas.

2. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas, zero external geometry libraries, zero emojis.
3. Add unit test `scripts/test-optics-prism-sandbox.js` verifying Snell's law refraction angle accuracy, Total Internal Reflection cutoff beyond critical angle `arcsin(n2/n1)`, and ray-segment intersection edge cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: [Feature/Core]: Fixed-Point Q16.16 Arithmetic Math Engine and Cross-Browser Lockstep Checksum Verifier
body:
## Problem
IEEE-754 floating-point math (`Math.sin`, `Math.cos`, `Math.sqrt`) can drift slightly across different CPU architectures and browsers, breaking deterministic game physics replays and lockstep multiplayer. ArcadeVerse lacks a zero-float fixed-point `Q16.16` math library and deterministic checksum verification harness.

## Architectural Scope & Requirements
1. **Substantial Implementation Scope (Minimum 280+ LOC):**
   - Create `assets/js/fixed-point-lockstep.js`:
     - Implement integer-only `Q16.16` fixed-point arithmetic (`SCALE = 65536`) using `Math.imul` / `BigInt`-safe 64-bit intermediate products for `mul`, `div`, integer `sqrt` (bitwise digit-by-digit), deterministic CORDIC / LUT `sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, and 2D fixed-point vector helpers (`Vec2FP`).
     - Implement deterministic Mulberry32/XorShift32 PRNG + CRC32 state-snapshot checksum (`crc32(int32Array)`) plus a live visual Demo Harness running twin physics-particle arenas side-by-side (Native Float vs Deterministic `Q16.16` Lockstep) verifying frame-by-frame checksum parity!
   - Create `assets/css/fixed-point-lockstep.css`:
     - Split simulation diagnostic panel showing side-by-side frame tick counters, live hex CRC32 state hashes (`0x8F3A19C2`), precision error delta vs `Math.sin`, and benchmark throughput comparison.
2. Pure Vanilla JS/2D Canvas, zero external math/crypto libraries, zero emojis.
3. Add comprehensive test suite `scripts/test-fixed-point-lockstep.js` validating `Q16.16` `mul`/`div` accuracy, integer `sqrt` exactness (`sqrt(fromInt(25)) === fromInt(5)`), CORDIC trig error bounds (`< 0.002`), overflow guards, and identical 1,000-tick CRC32 lockstep replay hashes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Integer-only `Q16.16` operations execute without `Math.sin`/`Math.cos`/`Math.sqrt` floating-point drift.
- [ ] Twin 1,000-frame lockstep simulation replays produce bit-exact matching CRC32 checksums every run.
- [ ] Unit tests verify arithmetic precision, division-by-zero guards, and trig accuracy rigorously.
- [ ] Codebase exceeds 280 meaningful lines across isolated files without editing protected core files.
- [ ] Test script `scripts/test-fixed-point-lockstep.js` passes cleanly under `node`.
